eras.name: VAEs and GANs
eras.blurb: Neural networks learn to generate. VAEs compress images to a latent space; GANs set a generator against a critic. Faces get photoreal, audio and the Transformer arrive.

eras.name: Diffusion appears, language models scale
eras.blurb: Score matching and DDPM turn denoising into a generator; GPT-3 shows scale and prompting; NeRF opens 3D.

source.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (Ho et al., 2020)

eras.name: Text meets image
eras.blurb: CLIP links words to pixels, DALL-E shows text prompts, diffusion beats GANs, and latent diffusion makes it affordable.

source.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision (Radford et al., 2021)

eras.name: Diffusion goes public
eras.blurb: Closed text-to-image systems arrive, then Stable Diffusion's open weights put the technology in everyone's hands. Guidance, personalisation, video and 3D follow within months.

source.title: Stable Diffusion Public Release (Stability AI, 22 Aug 2022)

eras.name: Control and open weights
eras.blurb: ControlNet and IP-Adapter add control, SDXL raises resolution, open language models appear, and open video starts.

source.title: Adding Conditional Control to Text-to-Image Diffusion Models (Zhang et al., 2023)

eras.name: Transformers, flow matching and open video
eras.blurb: The U-Net gives way to Transformers and flow matching: SD3 and FLUX. Sora sets a bar for video, and open video and image-to-3D models follow.

eras.name: Open models catch up
eras.blurb: Open weights reach or approach closed quality in video (Wan), images (Qwen-Image, Z-Image, FLUX.2), 3D and music, under permissive licences.

source.title: Wan: Open and Advanced Large-Scale Video Generative Models (Wan Team, 2025)

eras.name: Today
eras.blurb: Joint audio-video models, multi-reference editing and local-first tooling. Many 2026 dates here are Hugging Face repository dates, not announcements.

source.title: FLUX.2 repository: klein release, 15 Jan 2026 (Black Forest Labs)

models.name: Variational autoencoder (VAE)
models.what: Trains an encoder and a decoder together so images compress into a smooth latent space and can be sampled back out.
models.why: Every image and video model in this studio decodes its result through a VAE; the latent in latent diffusion starts here.

models.name: Generative adversarial networks (GAN)
models.what: Two networks train against each other: a generator forges samples and a discriminator tries to tell them from real data.
models.why: The first widely used way to generate sharp images, and the standard that diffusion models later had to beat.

models.name: Diffusion probabilistic model

source.title: Deep Unsupervised Learning using Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics

models.what: Builds a generative model by slowly destroying data with noise and learning to reverse each small step.
models.why: The first diffusion model. It was largely overlooked until DDPM in 2020.

models.name: DCGAN

source.title: Unsupervised Representation Learning with Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks

models.what: A convolutional GAN architecture with design rules that made GAN training reliable on images.
models.why: The recipe most later image GANs copied.

models.name: WaveNet

source.title: WaveNet: A Generative Model for Raw Audio

models.what: An autoregressive network that predicts raw audio one sample at a time with dilated convolutions.
models.why: Showed neural networks could generate natural speech and music directly as waveforms: the start of neural audio generation.

models.name: Transformer (Attention Is All You Need)
models.what: Replaces recurrence with self-attention so a model reads a whole sequence in parallel.
models.why: The architecture under today's language models and, through DiT, most of the image and video generators in this atlas.

models.name: VQ-VAE
models.what: A VAE whose latent code is a choice from a learned codebook instead of continuous numbers.
models.why: Turned images into token sequences a Transformer can model; the line runs to DALL-E and to latent diffusion's autoencoders.

models.name: BigGAN

source.title: Large Scale GAN Training for High Fidelity Natural Image Synthesis

models.what: Class-conditional GANs trained with very large batches and a truncation trick.
models.why: Showed GAN quality keeps improving with scale, at 512-pixel ImageNet resolution.

models.name: StyleGAN

source.title: A Style-Based Generator Architecture for Generative Adversarial Networks

models.what: A generator that injects a style vector at every layer, giving control from coarse to fine features.
models.why: Made photorealistic synthetic faces routine and editable.

models.name: Score-based generative modelling (NCSN)

source.title: Generative Modeling by Estimating Gradients of the Data Distribution

models.what: Learns the score, the direction in which data becomes more likely, at several noise levels and samples by following it.
models.why: The score-based route to diffusion; it merges with DDPM in 2020.

models.name: NeRF

source.title: NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis

models.what: A small network maps a 3D position and viewing direction to colour and density, trained from a set of photos.
models.why: Made photoreal new views from photos practical; text-to-3D methods such as DreamFusion build on it.

models.name: GPT-3
models.what: A 175-billion-parameter language model that follows examples given in its prompt.
models.why: Showed that scale alone gives in-context learning, the basis of prompting every model since.

models.name: DDPM
models.what: Trains a network to remove a little noise at each of about a thousand steps; sampling runs the chain backward from pure noise.
models.why: Showed diffusion can match the best GANs with a simple, stable loss: the template for every diffusion model here.

models.name: DDIM
models.what: A deterministic sampler for DDPM-trained models that skips steps.
models.why: Cut sampling from hundreds of steps to tens: the origin of fast samplers.

models.name: Frame interpolation (RIFE, FILM, GIMM-VFI)

source.title: Real-Time Intermediate Flow Estimation for Video Frame Interpolation

models.what: Models that insert frames between frames. The date is the RIFE paper's.

models.name: RIFE v4.9 (ONNX)

source.title: Real-Time Intermediate Flow Estimation for Video Frame Interpolation

models.what: RIFE real-time intermediate flow estimation for frame interpolation, in ONNX form.

models.name: Score SDE

source.title: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations

models.what: Describes diffusion as a stochastic differential equation and sampling as solving its reverse, unifying the score and DDPM views.
models.why: The maths behind samplers, schedulers and the later flow-matching view.

models.name: VQGAN (Taming Transformers)

source.title: Taming Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis

models.what: Combines a VQ autoencoder trained with a GAN and perceptual loss with an autoregressive Transformer.
models.why: Its perceptual compression is the autoencoder that latent diffusion reuses.

models.name: Face restoration (GFPGAN, CodeFormer, GPEN)

source.title: Towards Real-World Blind Face Restoration with Generative Facial Prior

models.what: Face restoration models. The date is the GFPGAN paper's; the others were not checked.

models.name: DALL-E (zero-shot text-to-image)
models.what: A 12-billion-parameter autoregressive Transformer over text tokens and image tokens.
models.why: First broad demonstration that a text prompt could steer a general image generator.

models.name: CLIP

source.title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision

models.what: Trains an image encoder and a text encoder so matching pictures and captions land close together.
models.why: CLIP text encoders condition Stable Diffusion 1.x and SDXL, and CLIP is a common way to score prompt match.

models.name: Diffusion models beat GANs

source.title: Diffusion Models Beat GANs on Image Synthesis

models.what: Architecture changes and classifier guidance that push diffusion past BigGAN on ImageNet.
models.why: The result that moved the field from GANs to diffusion.

models.name: LoRA

source.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

models.what: Freezes a model and trains small low-rank update matrices instead of the full weights.
models.why: Made fine-tuning cheap: most community styles and characters for the image and video models here ship as LoRAs.

models.name: Latent diffusion

source.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models

models.what: Runs diffusion in the compressed latent space of a pretrained autoencoder instead of in pixels, with cross-attention for text.
models.why: Cut the cost of high-resolution diffusion enough for consumer GPUs; the basis of Stable Diffusion.

models.name: Video diffusion models
models.what: Extends image diffusion to video with a 3D U-Net that denoises many frames at once.
models.why: An early diffusion model for video: the line to Sora and the open video models below.

models.name: DALL-E 2 (unCLIP)

source.title: Hierarchical Text-Conditional Image Generation with CLIP Latents

models.what: Generates a CLIP image embedding from the caption, then decodes it to pixels with diffusion.
models.why: Showed CLIP embeddings plus diffusion give photorealistic text-to-image.

models.name: Imagen

source.title: Photorealistic Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Deep Language Understanding

models.what: Text-to-image diffusion conditioned on a large frozen T5 language model.
models.why: Found that scaling the text encoder helps more than scaling the image model; SD3 and FLUX later use T5 too.

models.name: Classifier-free guidance
models.what: Trains one model with and without the prompt, then extrapolates between the two at sampling time.
models.why: The CFG scale in every workflow here is this.

models.name: Stable Diffusion 1.x
models.what: A latent diffusion text-to-image model with downloadable weights, released publicly by Stability AI under the CreativeML Open RAIL-M licence.
models.why: Anyone could run, fine-tune and modify it on a home GPU; the community of checkpoints, LoRAs and ComfyUI grew from it.

models.name: DreamBooth

source.title: DreamBooth: Fine Tuning Text-to-Image Diffusion Models for Subject-Driven Generation

models.what: Fine-tunes a text-to-image model on a few photos of one subject, tied to a rare token.
models.why: Started personalised models, which LoRA later made cheap.

models.name: Rectified flow and flow matching
models.org: Liu et al.; Lipman et al.

source.title: Flow Straight and Fast: Learning to Generate and Transfer Data with Rectified Flow

models.what: Learns straight-line paths between noise and data. Flow matching (arXiv 2210.02747, October 2022) gives the same idea a simulation-free training objective.
models.why: The training objective behind SD3, FLUX and Wan, and most models from 2024 on in this atlas.

models.name: DreamFusion
models.what: Optimises a NeRF so its renders score well under a frozen text-to-image diffusion model (score distillation).
models.why: Text-to-3D with no 3D training data.

models.name: Make-A-Video

source.title: Make-A-Video: Text-to-Video Generation without Text-Video Data

models.what: Text-to-video built from a text-to-image model plus unlabelled video, with no paired text-video data.
models.why: Showed video generation could be bootstrapped from image models.

models.name: ChatGPT
models.what: A conversational model trained with reinforcement learning from human feedback, released as a free research preview.
models.why: Brought language models to mainstream users.

models.name: DiT (diffusion Transformer)
models.what: Replaces the diffusion U-Net with a Transformer over latent patches.
models.why: Transformers scale predictably; SD3, FLUX, Wan, Qwen-Image and Z-Image all follow this design.

models.name: ControlNet

source.title: Adding Conditional Control to Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

models.what: Adds a trainable copy of an encoder that reads an edge, depth or pose map and steers a frozen diffusion model.
models.why: Gave artists precise control of composition; the pose, depth and edge control models in ComfyUI descend from it.

models.name: LLaMA

source.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models

models.what: A family of 7B to 65B language models trained on public data.
models.why: Its weights reached researchers and the community and started the open-weight language model wave.

models.name: Consistency models
models.what: Maps any point on a noise-to-data path straight to the clean image, allowing one- or few-step sampling.
models.why: A basis of few-step distillation; the 4-step and 8-step distilled checkpoints here use related ideas.

models.name: Shap-E
models.what: Generates the parameters of 3D implicit functions from text or an image.
models.why: An early open text-to-3D model with weights under the MIT licence.

models.name: LDM3D (4-channel)
models.what: A latent diffusion model that generates an RGB image and its depth map together.

models.name: MusicGen
models.what: A single Transformer over EnCodec audio tokens, conditioned on text or a melody.
models.why: An open text-to-music baseline; the released weights are non-commercial.

models.name: Llama 2

source.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models

models.what: Open-weight chat and base models from 7B to 70B parameters.
models.why: Allowed commercial use under a community licence, which brought open models into business use.

models.name: SDXL
models.date_basis: Stability AI release post (fetched); paper arXiv 2307.01952 is dated 2023-07-04
models.what: A latent diffusion model with a larger U-Net, two text encoders and a refinement stage, trained for 1024-pixel images.
models.why: The base for a large share of community checkpoints, LoRAs and ControlNets.

models.name: DWPose

source.title: Effective Whole-body Pose Estimation with Two-stages Distillation

models.what: Whole-body pose estimation with two-stage distillation; used to make pose control images.

models.name: 3D Gaussian splatting

source.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering

models.what: Represents a scene as millions of 3D Gaussians drawn by fast rasterisation.
models.why: Real-time photoreal scenes from photos; the main alternative to NeRF.

models.name: IP-Adapter

source.title: IP-Adapter: Text Compatible Image Prompt Adapter for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models

models.what: A small adapter that feeds image features into cross-attention so a picture acts like a prompt.
models.why: Image prompting, style and identity transfer without fine-tuning.

models.name: Mistral 7B
models.what: A 7B model with grouped-query and sliding-window attention.
models.why: The paper reports it outperforms Llama 2 13B on its benchmarks, under the Apache-2.0 licence.

models.name: Stable Video Diffusion

source.title: Stable Video Diffusion: Scaling Latent Video Diffusion Models to Large Datasets

models.what: A latent video diffusion model trained in stages on a curated video dataset; image-to-video weights were released.
models.why: An early widely used open image-to-video model.

models.name: Stable Cascade
models.what: A three-stage model built on the Wuerstchen architecture, working in a very compressed latent space.
models.why: Stability AI's post says the three-stage design makes it easy to train and fine-tune on consumer hardware.

models.name: Sora

source.title: Video generation models as world simulators

models.what: A diffusion Transformer over spacetime patches of video latents; the report says it can generate a minute of video.
models.why: Reset expectations for video quality and for the world-simulator framing that open video models chase.

models.name: TripoSR

source.title: TripoSR: Fast 3D Object Reconstruction from a Single Image

models.what: Fast 3D reconstruction of an object from a single image.
models.why: A small MIT-licensed image-to-3D model that runs in seconds on a desktop GPU is the paper's claim; this studio runs it as a family instance.

models.name: PixArt-Sigma

source.title: PixArt-Σ: Weak-to-Strong Training of Diffusion Transformer for 4K Text-to-Image Generation

models.what: Weak-to-strong training of a diffusion Transformer for 4K text-to-image.

models.name: InstantMesh

source.title: InstantMesh: Efficient 3D Mesh Generation from a Single Image with Sparse-view Large Reconstruction Models

models.what: Efficient 3D mesh generation from a single image with a sparse-view reconstruction model.

models.name: Hunyuan-DiT

source.title: Hunyuan-DiT: A Powerful Multi-Resolution Diffusion Transformer with Fine-Grained Chinese Understanding

models.what: A multi-resolution diffusion Transformer with fine-grained Chinese understanding.

models.name: Kolors
models.what: Kuaishou's text-to-image model.

models.name: Stable Diffusion 3 and 3.5
models.date_basis: Stability AI release post (fetched); paper arXiv 2403.03206 is dated 2024-03-05
models.what: A multimodal diffusion Transformer trained with rectified flow and three text encoders. SD3 Medium weights came in June 2024, SD 3.5 in October 2024.
models.why: Moved Stability AI's line from the U-Net to Transformers and flow matching.

models.name: Stable Fast 3D
models.what: Fast single-image 3D mesh generation from Stability AI.

models.name: FLUX.1
models.what: A 12B-parameter flow-matching Transformer with parallel attention blocks, released as [pro] (API), [dev] (open weights, non-commercial) and [schnell] (Apache-2.0).
models.why: Raised the open-weight bar for image detail, text and prompt following.

models.name: CogVideoX
models.licence_note: 2B is Apache-2.0; the 5B has its own licence on the model card.

source.title: CogVideoX: Text-to-Video Diffusion Models with An Expert Transformer

models.what: Expert-Transformer text-to-video models with a 3D causal VAE, in 2B and 5B sizes.
models.why: Its README says the 2B model runs on a GTX 1080 Ti and the 5B on an RTX 3060, so open video reached desktop GPUs.

models.name: Allegro
models.what: An open text-to-video model from Rhymes AI.

models.name: Mochi 1
models.what: A 10-billion-parameter asymmetric diffusion Transformer trained from scratch.
models.why: Released under Apache-2.0; its README calls it the largest openly released video model at the time.

models.name: LTX-Video
models.date_basis: Lightricks README: initial release v0.9.0 (fetched); paper arXiv 2501.00103 is dated 2024-12-30
models.what: A Transformer video model with a highly compressed video VAE, aimed at real-time generation.
models.why: Showed open video generation could run near real time; the line continues as LTX-2.5 below.

models.name: TRELLIS

source.title: Structured 3D Latents for Scalable and Versatile 3D Generation

models.what: Generates 3D assets from text or an image through structured 3D latents decoded to Gaussians, radiance fields or meshes.
models.why: A common starting point for open image-to-3D pipelines; TRELLIS.2 follows in 2025.

models.name: HunyuanVideo
models.date_basis: Tencent README: code and weights released (fetched)
models.what: Tencent's open video foundation model with a systematic data-to-inference framework.
models.why: Open weights for a large text-to-video model, adapted widely after release (Diffusers support and FP8 weights followed within two weeks).

models.name: FitDiT
models.what: A garment virtual try-on model.

models.name: DeepSeek-R1
models.date_basis: Hugging Face repo created; paper arXiv 2501.12948 is dated 2025-01-22

source.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning

models.what: A reasoning model trained with large-scale reinforcement learning.
models.why: Open weights under the MIT licence for a reasoning model.

models.name: Lumina-Image 2.0
models.date_basis: Hugging Face repo created; paper arXiv 2503.21758 is dated 2025-03-27

source.title: Lumina-Image 2.0: A Unified and Efficient Image Generative Framework

models.what: A unified, efficient image generation framework.

models.name: Wan 2.1
models.date_basis: Wan2.1 README: inference code and weights released (fetched)

source.title: Wan: Open and Advanced Large-Scale Video Generative Models

models.what: Alibaba's open video suite: text-to-video at 1.3B and 14B and image-to-video, with a custom VAE. The README says the 1.3B model needs about 8 GB of VRAM.
models.why: Apache-2.0 video that the authors report ahead of other open models; the base for many LoRAs and for Wan 2.2.

models.name: MIDI-3D
models.what: Single image to compositional 3D scene generation with multi-instance diffusion.

models.name: YuE

source.title: YuE: Scaling Open Foundation Models for Long-Form Music Generation

models.what: An open lyrics-to-song foundation model that makes long songs with vocals and accompaniment.
models.why: Open weights under Apache-2.0 for full songs; YuE2 follows in 2026.

models.name: HiDream-I1 and O1

source.title: HiDream-I1: A High-Efficient Image Generative Foundation Model with Sparse Diffusion Transformer

models.what: HiDream-I1 (April 2025) is a sparse diffusion Transformer image model. HiDream-O1-Image (May 2026) is a pixel-space unified model with no separate VAE or text encoder.
models.why: MIT-licensed, so it can be used commercially.

models.name: UniRig

source.title: One Model to Rig Them All: Diverse Skeleton Rigging with UniRig

models.what: Automatic skeleton rigging for diverse 3D models.

models.name: Cosmos-Predict2 14B text-to-image
models.what: An NVIDIA Cosmos-Predict2 text-to-image checkpoint (14B).

models.name: Qwen3
models.what: Qwen's third-generation language models: dense models from 0.6B to 32B and two mixture-of-experts models.
models.why: Open weights under Apache-2.0 at every size.

models.name: PartCrafter

source.title: PartCrafter: Structured 3D Mesh Generation via Compositional Latent Diffusion Transformers

models.what: Structured 3D mesh generation of separate parts from one image with compositional latent diffusion Transformers.

models.name: SeedVR2

source.title: SeedVR2: One-Step Video Restoration via Diffusion Adversarial Post-Training

models.what: One-step video restoration through diffusion adversarial post-training.

models.name: Hunyuan3D 2.1
models.what: Image-to-3D with a shape model and a physically based (PBR) texture model.
models.why: Textured PBR assets that drop into game and DCC tools.

models.name: FLUX.1 Kontext

source.title: FLUX.1 Kontext: Flow Matching for In-Context Image Generation and Editing in Latent Space

models.what: In-context image editing and generation: an input image plus an instruction gives an edited image.
models.why: Made instruction-based editing with consistent characters an open-weight workflow ([dev], non-commercial).

models.name: OmniGen2
models.what: Instruction-aligned multimodal generation: text-to-image, editing and in-context generation.

models.name: HunyuanWorld 1.0
models.what: Generates explorable 3D worlds from words or pixels.

models.name: Wan 2.2
models.what: Alibaba's second-generation open video models. This studio runs the 5B text-and-image-to-video model for its Video and Animate goals, and the Fun Camera model for reshoots.
models.why: Apache-2.0 video the studio renders locally at 480p to 720p.

models.name: Qwen-Image
models.what: Alibaba Qwen's open image foundation model.
models.why: Apache-2.0, and the base of the Qwen-Image 2.x line below.

models.name: gpt-oss
models.what: OpenAI's open-weight reasoning models gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b.
models.why: Open weights under Apache-2.0; the 120b fits one 80 GB GPU and the 20b runs in 16 GB of memory, per OpenAI.

models.name: Matrix-Game 2.0
models.what: A 1.8B interactive world model that generates long videos on the fly with few-step autoregressive diffusion.

models.name: Wan 2.2 Animate 14B
models.what: Character animation and replacement from a reference video, built on Wan 2.2.

models.name: SANA-Video
models.what: Efficient video generation from the Efficient-Large-Model group.

models.name: FlashVSR 1.1
models.what: Diffusion-based video super-resolution.

models.name: Kandinsky 5.0 T2I Lite
models.what: A 6B text-to-image model (latent diffusion with flow matching) from the Kandinsky 5.0 family.

models.name: SAM 3D Objects
models.what: Meta's model that reconstructs 3D objects from a single image.
models.why: Single-photo 3D with checkpoints released in November 2025.

models.name: FLUX.2 [dev]
models.what: A 32B-parameter model for text-to-image and editing with single and multiple reference images.
models.why: Open weights under the FLUX Non-Commercial License.

models.name: Z-Image
models.date_basis: Hugging Face repo created (Turbo); paper arXiv 2511.22699 is dated 2025-11-27

source.title: Z-Image: An Efficient Image Generation Foundation Model with Single-Stream Diffusion Transformer

models.what: A 6B-parameter single-stream diffusion Transformer family; Z-Image-Turbo is distilled to 8 function evaluations.
models.why: A small, fast, Apache-2.0 image model for consumer cards.

models.name: Ovis-Image 7B
models.what: A 7B text-to-image model.

models.name: TRELLIS.2
models.what: Microsoft's 4B-parameter successor to TRELLIS for image-to-3D.
models.why: MIT-licensed image-to-3D that this studio can run as a family instance.

models.name: LongCat-Image
models.what: A 6B bilingual (Chinese and English) text-to-image model with strong Chinese text rendering.

models.name: HY-Motion 1.0
models.what: Text-to-3D human motion generation with a diffusion Transformer and flow matching.

models.name: FLUX.2 [klein]
models.what: A family of fast FLUX.2 models: 4B and 9B, distilled and base. Black Forest Labs' README says sub-second generation on consumer GPUs. The 4B is Apache-2.0; the 9B is non-commercial.
models.why: The model behind this studio's Image goal.

models.name: ACE-Step 1.5
models.what: An open music generation foundation model. Version 1 (April 2025, Apache-2.0) is described in arXiv 2506.00045; 1.5 followed in January 2026.
models.why: Local song generation that runs as a family instance here.

models.name: Anima
models.what: A 2B text-to-image model for anime and non-photorealistic art, made by CircleStone Labs with Comfy Org.
models.why: The studio's Anime goal.

models.name: MOVA

source.title: MOVA: Towards Scalable and Synchronized Video-Audio Generation

models.what: Open video-and-audio generation with an asymmetric dual-tower design (32B mixture of experts, 18B active).

models.name: PixelDiT
models.licence: NVIDIA licence nsclv1 (see the model card)
models.what: A VAE-free pixel diffusion Transformer with patch-level and pixel-level stages and a Gemma-2-2B text encoder.

models.name: ERNIE-Image
models.what: Baidu's open text-to-image model, a single-stream diffusion Transformer.

models.name: Pixal3D
models.what: Pixel-aligned 3D generation from a single image (SIGGRAPH 2026).

models.name: LongCat-Video-Avatar 1.5
models.what: Audio-driven human video generation: audio-text-to-video, audio-text-image-to-video and video continuation.

models.name: Ideogram 4
models.what: Ideogram's text-to-image model, with open weights on Hugging Face.

models.name: SCAIL-2
models.what: End-to-end controlled character animation: animates a reference character with a driving video, and supports replacement and multi-character scenes.

models.name: Boogu-Image 0.1
models.what: Open image generation and editing models (Base, Edit, Edit-Turbo).

models.name: Krea 2

models.licence_note: Free below a revenue threshold set in the licence; larger organisations need a paid licence.

models.why: The studio's Video + sound, Animate + sound and VFX goals.

models.name: MiniMax H3
models.licence_note: The licence's territory is worldwide excluding the European Union, the United Kingdom, the Republic of Korea and the United States of America (clauses 3 and 5, read from the licence file). Read it before use.

models.why: The studio's Video H3, Animate H3, Recast, Reshoot and Director goals.

models.name: SeFi-Image 2B turbo
models.what: A 2B turbo text-to-image model; the model card has no description.

models.name: JoyAI-Video-Edit

models.name: MiniMax Music 3
models.licence: Not stated in the upstream card metadata; the Comfy-Org repackage is tagged Apache-2.0. Read the upstream LICENSE.
models.what: Full songs up to five minutes from lyrics and a music description: an 8B global LM, a 0.6B local LM and a flow-matching synthesis stage, 32 kHz stereo.
models.why: The studio's Music goal.

models.name: Qwen3.8
models.what: Qwen's August 2026 models; this studio's top crew LLM tier runs the 27B FP8 build with vLLM.
models.why: Apache-2.0.

models.name: DreamX-Creator 1.0
models.what: A research framework for native joint audio-video generation: a 7B base generator and a one-step 2K refiner.

models.name: YuE2 3B
models.what: Open music generation, with text-to-music and music-cover workflows.

models.name: Qwen-Image 2.1

models.name: Ming-Image 0.1 Design
models.what: A 6B text-to-image model for UI, infographics, posters and other text-rich designs, with transparent RGBA output.

models.name: Iris-3B
